the development of a method for the reconstruction of the aortic root with a tricuspidisation procedure.
the development of an artificial tricuspid aortic valve with a crown-like annular ring and the evaluation of the valve function in vitro.
the development of a new surgical procedure, the tricuspidisation of bicuspid aortas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aortic root dilatation is not a consequence of the aortic regurgitation.

the aortic valve is a complex structure that can be described by the presence of three cusps, the size of these cusps and the presence of any other abnormalities such as calcifications, fibrosis and/or regurgitation.
aortic valve replacement is the treatment of choice for aortic regurgitation in the setting of aortic valve endocarditis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results from the present study indicate that the combination of aortic and mitral regurgitation is an independent predictor of mortality and that aortic regurgitation should be considered a risk factor when assessing patients undergoing mitral valve repair.
the use of aortic valve replacement with tricuspidization in bicuspid valve disease is a safe and effective procedure.
the aortic valve is a dynamic structure that is capable of adaptation to the changing haemodynamic environment and is not simply a passive barrier to blood flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tricuspidisation of bicuspid aortics is feasible with a high degree of success, and that the technique has a low risk of complications and a low mortality.
the tricuspidization procedure can restore a normal valve structure and function in bicusupid aortic valves, and that this can be achieved without a prosthetic valve.
tricuspidisation of a bicuspid aorta is a safe procedure and can be performed with a low complication rate.
